mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real personal consumption (measured by RSAFS) directly increases corporate earnings growth expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS growth is positive, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, causing immediate negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through their joint effect.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions characterized by high consumer confidence (measured by RSAFS growth above 1.5% annually), demand-driven S&P 500 returns become positive over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansions (RSAFS growth > 1.5% annually), or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% annually signals persistent inflation that typically leads to delayed monetary policy responses, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate future rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL growth exceeds 3.0% annually, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates a tight labor market that accelerates wage growth and consumer spending, causing immediate negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to inflation fears.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% for 2 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS signals an active monetary tightening cycle that reduces real interest rates and equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through their joint effect.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both rise, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1.6 million units annually, it indicates strong residential investment that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1.6 million units annually, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.
